structs.size_evidence: NOT PROVEN. Lower bound 132: GTurretMP::SpawnVirtual@0x1410117B0 writes int at +128 (`*(_DWORD *)(this + 128) = 0`, last byte 131). Upper bound candidate 256 (game-test GTurretMP 256, game-test GTurret 256): GTurretMP::vector_deleting_dtor@0x1405C5F30 stores GTurretMP_vftable at [rcx] and, when flags bit 0 is set, `mov edx, 100h` / `call bdMemory::deallocate_5` at 0x1405C5F48. That function is vtable slot 1 of GTurretMP_vftable (0x1427468C8, xref from .rdata). BLOCKER: slot 0 of the same vtable, Dtor8_scalar_deleting_Vt7468B8@0x1405C5E90, also stores GTurretMP_vftable but frees with `mov edx, 8` (0x1405C5EA8), so the vtable does not give one consistent object size. structs.notes: Verdict partial because the size is contested (slot 0 frees 8, slot 1 frees 256, same vtable) and no GTurretMP allocation is reachable. Size could be 256 if slot 1 is the true class dtor, but the constructor that stores GTurretMP_vftable is not in this database (only the two dtors). Next step for a follow-up: find who calls GTurretMP's vtable-owning allocation (e.g. a turret pool in a G_Main*AllocateGameMemory path with a computed stride), or resolve which dtor is GTurretMP's. The 1032-byte IDA size is not supported by any Replay access. GTurretMP::vector_deleting_dtor has no array loop, so the 'vector' name is also doubtful; see renames. vtable GTurretMP_vftable is three meaningful slots: [0] Dtor8, [1] vector_deleting_dtor, [2] _purecall; slot 3 at 0x1427468D0 is MultiProcessIndex_BuildFreeSpaceTableSignaled (a different function, not a turret virtual), so the table ends at slot 2. GTurretMP::SpawnVirtual, ThinkVirtual, SetMinimapVisible are not in this table.

renames: slot 0 of GTurretMP_vftable (0x1427468B8, xref from .rdata); the function stores GTurretMP_vftable at [rcx] and has the scalar flags-bit-0 deallocate. Name has the vtable address baked in. NOTE: its deallocate size is 8, which conflicts with the 256 of slot 1; the rename rests on the vtable store, not the size
